title: Catalpol enhances mTORC1/HIF-1alpha/PDHK1-mediated oxidative metabolism that leads to promote the differentiation of Treg cells in RA.
authors: Zhang, Qiaoyu; Wang, Furong; Ding, Peng; Ge, Yu; Bao, Yujie; Jiang, Baoping; Zhou, Lingling
one_liner_zh: 该文研究中药梓醇通过mTORC1/HIF-1alpha/PDHK1通路促进Treg分化治疗类风湿关节炎，仅涉及分子对接预测，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合位点或AI/物理模拟建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease in which regulatory T (Treg) cell dysfunction contributes to its pathogenesis, although the mechanisms regulating Treg differentiation remain unclear. In this study, the effects of Catalpol (CAT) on Treg differentiation and its underlying mechanisms were investigated using a CIA mouse model, with animals randomly allocated to CIA, CIA+CAT, and No CIA groups. Synovial pathology was assessed by HE staining, while naive CD4(+) T cells were differentiated into Tregs in vitro, and treated with CAT. Molecular docking predicted CAT-target interactions, and the mTORC1 activator NV5138 was used alongside CAT for intervention. Treg proportions and mitochondrial membrane potential were analyzed by flow cytometry, IL-10 levels were measured by ELISA, NAD(+)/NADH was detected by assay kit, and mRNA expression of FOXP3, mTOR, Raptor, HIF-1alpha, and PDHK1 were determined by RT-qPCR, while protein expression was assessed by Western blotting. The results demonstrated that CAT alleviated joint symptoms in CIA mice, promoted Treg differentiation both in vivo and in vitro, and increased mitochondrial membrane potential, NAD(+)/NADH and acetyl-CoA levels in Tregs. CAT also downregulated HIF-1alpha and PDHK1 mRNA and inhibited p-P70S6K/P70S6K, p-4EBP1/4EBP1, HIF-1alpha, and PDHK1 protein expression. Treatment with NV5138 was observed to reduce Treg differentiation and oxidative metabolism, effects which were reversed by CAT. These findings demonstrate that CAT promotes Treg differentiation and exerts anti-RA effects through inhibition of the mTORC1/HIF-1alpha/PDHK1 signaling pathway and enhancement of pyruvate aerobic oxidation.
abstract_zh: 类风湿关节炎（rheumatoid arthritis, RA）是一种慢性自身免疫性疾病，其中调节性T（regulatory T, Treg）细胞功能障碍参与其发病机制，尽管调控Treg分化的机制仍不清楚。本研究利用CIA小鼠模型，探讨了梓醇（Catalpol, CAT）对Treg分化的影响及其潜在机制，动物被随机分配至CIA、CIA+CAT和No CIA组。通过HE染色评估滑膜病理，同时在体外将初始CD4(+) T细胞分化为Tregs，并用CAT处理。分子对接预测了CAT与靶标的相互作用，并联合使用mTORC1激活剂NV5138与CAT进行干预。通过流式细胞术分析Treg比例和线粒体膜电位，ELISA检测IL-10水平，试剂盒检测NAD(+)/NADH，RT-qPCR测定FOXP3、mTOR、Raptor、HIF-1alpha和PDHK1的mRNA表达，Western blotting评估蛋白表达。结果表明，CAT缓解了CIA小鼠的关节症状，在体内和体外均促进了Treg分化，并增加了Tregs中的线粒体膜电位、NAD(+)/NADH和乙酰辅酶A水平。CAT还下调了HIF-1alpha和PDHK1 mRNA，并抑制了p-P70S6K/P70S6K、p-4EBP1/4EBP1、HIF-1alpha和PDHK1蛋白表达。观察到NV5138处理减少了Treg分化和氧化代谢，这些效应被CAT逆转。这些发现表明，CAT通过抑制mTORC1/HIF-1alpha/PDHK1信号通路并增强丙酮酸有氧氧化，促进Treg分化并发挥抗RA作用。
